messages:
ava: Heads-up — running into flaky trace links for batched jobs that go through the gateway -> kafka -> worker chain. When a single user request fans out into a batch of background jobs we lose parent/span continuity. Anyone have a lightweight encoding pattern we can standardize on for OTEL context in message attributes?

sahil: which queue type? kafka headers are binary-safe; SQS/message-attrs are limited. are we talking SQS, kinesis, or kafka?

ava: mostly kafka for high-throughput, but also SQS for some customers. need something that works for both.

marta: We used to just ship the W3C traceparent header as a string in `traceparent` attr. That works for spans but we lost baggage. Also some older consumers strip unknown headers.

josh: FWIW OTEL has a text format for propagation (W3C + baggage). But binary context (protobuf) is more compact. For SQS we base64 the binary and put it in a message-attribute string field: `x-otlp-b64`. cheap and interoperable.

ava: can you paste the base64 example?

josh: Sure — roughly: ```python
# producer
span_ctx = tracer.get_current_span().get_context()
serialized = http_text_format_injector.serialize(span_ctx)  # or otlp-proto bytes
msg.attrs['x-otlp-b64'] = base64.b64encode(serialized).decode('ascii')

# consumer
raw = base64.b64decode(msg.attrs.get('x-otlp-b64'))
ctx = injector.deserialize(raw)
with tracer.use_span(ctx):
    do_work()
```

marta: Two caveats: 1) message size limits — ensure we don't exceed attr size (SQS has limits). 2) We need consistent serializer across services (HTTP-text vs OTLP-proto).

ava: For kafka headers, do we still base64 or put raw bytes?

josh: Kafka headers are bytes, so raw bytes ok. But for consistency and easier debugging I still like a `traceparent` text header + optional `x-otlp-b64` for full state. That lets quick tooling read traceparent without decoding.

sahil: From infra perspective we need a fallback when header missing: create a synthetic parent with tag `origin:fanout` and include `fanout.batch_id`. That lets traces stitch in the UI without breaking.

marta: Also consider sampling implications — if root request is unsampled, the batch jobs may be unsampled. We should propagate sampling decision explicitly. Add `ot-sampled: 1` or use traceflags in traceparent.

ava: Good point — we had gaps where jobs were sampled and parent was not, causing orphaned high-cardinality traces.

josh: On exporters/retention: our current jaeger backend expires traces at 7 days. For batches/debugging we sometimes want 30d. Maybe route high-error traces to long-retention storage (tempo/long-term) and keep normal at 7d. We'll need a trace-processor rule keyed on `error==true` or `origin==fanout`.

marta: Agree. We can add a downstream processor that marks `rt.retention=30d` on spans matching policies. OTEL collector supports routing processors, but watch cardinality.

sahil: Ops note: can't arbitrarily increase retention for everything — cost. Let's keep a policy: retain errors and traces triggered by `debug=true` query param, plus on-demand capture endpoint.

ava: UX idea for console: when a request spawns N jobs, show a “fanout tree” in trace view and include the batch_id and a link to related job traces. That will make debugging way easier.

marta: Implementation detail: add `x-fanout-batch` attribute on every message containing UUID and parent trace id. That way the UI can query by `batch_id` and assemble parallel spans.

josh: For rollout plan: 1) standardize serializer (text traceparent + optional proto-b64) 2) deploy consumer libs across services (canary on 10% services) 3) enable collector routing rule for `origin==fanout` to add retention tag 4) console changes to visualize batch.

ava: Sounds good. Quick checklist: which repo gets the helper lib? infra/trace-utils? and who owns canary? @sahil

sahil: I'll own canary. Put helper lib in eng-platform/trace-utils. Keep it tiny, MIT, and publish to internal pip/npm.

marta: I'll draft the OTEL collector config snippet for routing. Will paste here once done. :sparkles:

ava: Thanks all — I'll spin up a proposal doc and link to the helper lib once it's created. :thumbsup:
